3. The plaint case is that the suit land originally belonged to Abdul Baki Mollah. Defendant Nos. 4 to 6 got 88 decimals of land from RS khatian No. 818 by purchase from the successive heirs of Abdul Baki Mollah. Defendant No. 7, Asmat Ali Mollah got the said land by lease by patta dated 18-2-54 at a jama of Rs. 3 and 10 annas from defendant Nos. 1 to 4 and paid rent and possessed the same within the knowledge of defendant Nos. 1 to 3 and others. Defendant No. 7 sold the same to defendant Nos. 8 and 9 by registered kabala dated 17-4-56. Maim Bibi, wife of Asgar Ali Skeikh of Salimpur Mouza was owner of 0.27 acres of land from RS Plot No. 205 under RS khatian No. 118 by way of inheritance and she leased the said land to defendant No. 10 by registered patta dated 28-3-55 at a Jama of 15 annas, who sold it to defendant No. 8 and 9 by registered kabala dated 18-4-56. In this way, defendant Nos. 8 and 9 got 1.15 acres of land by purchase from RS plot Nos. 163, 175, 204 and 205. These defendants sold the suit land to plaintiffs by kabala dated 25-10-56 (schedule kha land) and plaintiffs are in peaceful pos-session of the said land. Defendant Nos. 1 to 3 in collusion with defendant Nos. 4 to 7 threatened to dispossess the plaintiffs from the suit land in Magh, 1376 RS, hence the suit. 

 4. Defendant No. 3 contested the suit and his specific case is that Abdul Baki Mollah transferred the land of RS khatian No. 118 in favour of his wife Fuljan by a registered Heba-bil Ewaj dated 16-2-45 to pay her dower money. Fuljan died and her heirs leased out the said land to defendant No. 7, Asmat Ali Molla by a registered Kabuliyat dated 26-11-52 at a jama of Rs. 8 and paisa 75 (Rs. 8.75). Defendant No. 7 thereafter leased the said land to defendant No. 3 by registered patta dated 28-4-53 at a jama of Rs. 7 and 2 Annas. Defendant No. 3 paid rents and possessed the same and his name was correctly recorded in the record of right and he paid rent to the government and got Dakhilas. Defendant No. 1 and 2 are contractors. They converted the suit land to a brick filed by paying compensation to defendant No. 3's bargadar. Defendant No. 7, a very cunning man, set up the plaintiffs to file this false suit and, as such, the same is liable to be dismissed. 

 13. Now I am to find out whether there was any fraudulent representation in executing the deed, that is, exhibit 1(d) and exhibit 1(a). The judgment of the trial Court is rubbish. I do not know how gentleman passed this order. He has no knowledge of writing out a judgment of an original suit. The only judgment to be considered i.e. the judgment of the Court of appeal below. In this suit it is admitted by the parties Abdul Barik Mollah was original owner of the land of RS Khatian No. 118 of mouza Sripur. Abdul Barik Mollah by a registered Heba-bill-Ewaj deed dated 16-1-45, exhibit-E, transferred the land to his wife, Fuljan Bibi to satisfy her dower debt. It is also submitted position Fuljan died leaving her husband Abdul Batik Mollah (PW 2), 4 sons and one daughter, Maina Bibi. Certain facts of this suit is not disputed, that is, defendant No. 7, Asmat Ali Mollah took lease of 3.10 acres of land including 0.90 acres covered by 20 decimals of land from Plot No. 176, 29 decimals of land from Plot No. 204 and 27 decimals of land from Plot No. 205 by registered kabuliyat dated 26-11-52, that is, in total 90 decimals of lands at a jama of Rs 8.75 (Rupees eight paisa seventy five) from the heirs of Fuljan Bibi by exhibit-C. It is also not disputed while the kabuliyat, exhibit-C, was executed and registered, Aftab Mondal, Aminuddin Mondal and Mainanessa were minors and since these recipients were minors, exhibit-C cannot be taken to be a valid document. From exhibits-1 and 1 (A), it appears defendant Nos. 4 got 88 decimals of land, which includes 20 decimals of land from RS Plot No. 163, 39 decimals of land from RS khatian No. 118 of Sripur Mouza and it is found from exhibit 2 (a), that is, Asmat Ali Mullah took lease of 20 decimals of land from RS Plot No. 163, 24 decimals of land from RS Plot No. 204 of RS khatian No. 118. From the aforesaid admitted facts it appears. Asmat Ali Mollah took lease of 90 decimals of land from RS khatian No. 118 by kabuliyat, exhibit-C and 73 decimals of land from said RS khatian No. 118 by patta exhibit 2 (a). This probably has been done to overcome difficulty, that is, if exhibit-C was not found valid, then defendant No. 7 took recourse of exhibit 2 (a). Asmat Ali Mollah sold 20 decimals of land from RS plot No. 163, 24 decimals of land from Plot No. 175 and 29 decimals of land from RS Plot No. 204 of RS khatian No. 118 by registered kabala dated 17-6-56 to defendant Nos. 8 and 9. This Asmat Ali Mollah leased out 20 decimals of land from Plot No. 175, 29 decimals of land from Plot No. 203 and 27 decimals of land from Plot No. 205 and other lands, totaling 1.55 acres of land to contesting defendant No. 3 by patta dated 28-4-1953, exhibit-A. In this point, the trial Court abruptly made a finding that the plaintiff got right, title and interest to the suit land and possession. The appellate Court here applied the principle of feeding the grant by estoppels as per provision of section 43 of the Transfer of Property Act. It has already been discussed above that there must be some evidence in taking recourse to the provision of section 43 of the Transfer of Property Act. It must be in the pleadings of the parties that transferor or the vendor made a fraudulent representation of erroneous act by which the transferee or the vendee believed him and entered into the transaction. It might be gathered from the facts of the case but unless there is specific pleadings by tither of the parties or there being no such intention disclosed in any of the documents or any evidence, the Court cannot of its own, applied this provision in any case. Learned Subordinate Judge without considering the recital of exhibit 1(d) to the effect exhibit-A, on his own motion, applied this provision of law. It has already been observed that there must be a fraudulent act on the part of the transferor and there must be some evidence as to option on the part of transferee. Now, I am to see how the Court of appeal below applied this provision of this doctrine, that is, feeding the grant by estoppels in the facts of the given case. Learned Judge after narrating the case of the parties, without discussing either of the aforesaid exhibits-1 (a) and A, held as follows; 

 14. There is no discussion as to how the fraudulent activities on the part of the vendor of Exhibit- 1(d) or to that effect exhibit-A and as to whether these two exhibits contends any such indication by which the Court is bound to apply section 43 of the Transfer of Property Act, applied this section. It has already been found that exhibit-C is a void document because three of the recipients, that is, Aftab Mondal, Aminuddin Mondal and Moinanessa were minors. Asmat Ali Mollah acquired the property through this exhibit-C, thereafter transferred it to defendant No. 3 by exhibit-A. On consideration of exhibit-A, I find it does not contends any statement by which it can be ascertained when it was made, Asmat Ali Mollah, the vendor, had any perfect title or not. It shows Asmat Ali Mollah have title over the transferred land of Amal Krishna Chandra. There is no recital as to how Asmat Ali Mollah acquired title. Since acquisition of title by Asmat Ali Mollah through exhibit-C having been found to be not valid, as the deed itself is a void document, defendant No. 3 by purchase from Asmat Ali Mollah did not acquire any title over the suit land. So, I find Learned Judge misapplied the provision of section 43 of the Transfer of Property Act on the facts of the instant case. On consideration of exhibit-1 (d), which is a registered document dated 17-6-56 by Asmat Ali Mollah in favour of plaintiff, I find it was later document then exhibit-A. Exhibit-A was registered on 28-4-53 and exhibit-2 (a) dated 18-2-54, I find Asmat Ali Mollah purchased the land from Akbar Ali, Anwar Hossain and Abul Hossain, that is, defendant Nos. 4 to 6, transferred 73 decimals of land and from exhibit-1 (e) I find defendant Nos. 8 and 9 transferred 73 decimals of land, which they acquired, to Asmat Ali Mollah. The plaintiff filed certified copy of khatian No. 118 as exhibit-3. From reading exhibit-C, I do not find any recited to find transferor make any option as provided under section 43 of the Transfer Property Act. The learned Advocate for the respondents desparately submits there was no issue framed by the learned Munsif as to maintainability of the suit. He further submits plaintiff failed to prove his possession, both orally and documentary and the trial Court did not discuss the evidence at length. I do not dispute as I have already mentioned the judgment of trial Court is rubbish.
